title: Replace hand parsed sys.argv with Click
summary: A script that writes a file called -v when the flag comes first moves to Click arguments and options, then IntRange bounds the limit.

files.content:
import csv
import sys


def fetch_users(limit):
    return [(i, f"user{i}") for i in range(limit)]


def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if not args:
        print("usage: export.py OUTPUT [--limit N] [--verbose]")
        sys.exit(1)
    output = args[0]
    limit = 100
    if "--limit" in args:
        limit = int(args[args.index("--limit") + 1])
    verbose = "--verbose" in args or "-v" in args
    rows = fetch_users(limit)
    with open(output, "w", newline="") as f:
        csv.writer(f).writerows(rows)
    if verbose:
        print(f"wrote {len(rows)} rows to {output}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

turns.user: the arg parsing in export.py is hand rolled and painful. put -v first and you get a file named -v lol. switch it to click

assistant.body: Great call! The current code hard codes args[0] as the output path, so a leading -v becomes the file name. With Click you declare the positional with @click.argument and the flags with @click.option, and the order on the command line stops mattering. default=100 makes Click infer int, so a value that is not a number is rejected for you. --help is generated too, so the hand written usage line is just boilerplate and can go.

turns.user: nice. let me write -n too. also --limit 0 or negative numbers get through, block those

assistant.body: Pass click.IntRange(min=1) as the type and Click reports anything below 1 as out of range. The short name is one more string, "-n", on the same option. In other words, the validation and the help text both live in the one declaration.
